title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples

bias_targets.methodology: Conditioning the language model on first-person demographic backstories that include political affiliation and ideology to generate descriptions of outgroup partisans and predict voting behavior, then comparing the output distributions to real human survey data (e.g., ANES).

Using 'silicon sampling' to condition the model on different racial and ethnic identities, evaluating how well the model replicates human correlations between race, political attitudes, and voting choices.
Inserting gender identities into the conditioning prompts to measure how accurately the model reproduces the correlation between gender and simulated political survey responses.
Conditioning the model on specific income and education levels to assess their influence on the model's simulated voting predictions and public opinion responses.
Including age brackets in the demographic conditioning templates to evaluate pattern correspondence in the simulated human voting behavior and survey answers.
Using church attendance and religiosity as conditioning variables in first-person prompts to assess how well the model replicates human political and behavioral correlations.
